summary: The 60 supplied occurrences were checked against full verses. Active human removal, accidental loss and annihilation all fit the existing II.1 gloss; no existing gloss text has been rewritten.

Repeated bare mḏ̣ayəʕ/mḏ̣ayʕo/mḏ̣ayʕi predicates occur after motion events and in reports of a missing state. The added Preterit filing is a reasoned proposal based on that distribution and the masculine/feminine/plural series, not a settled paradigm claim; unprefixed Infectum remains an alternative for some tokens.

Part. Pass. mḏ̣ayʕo no in PrS 65/39 is separated from bare finite candidates. First-person feminine mḏ̣ayʕono in PrS 44/59 may likewise involve a copular or finite analysis; the editors should compare both.
Final-ḥ forms and mzayʕo have not been silently emended or used to establish a box. Their analyses are rejected as secure evidence pending source checking.

Detransitive disappearance can conceal intentional removal: PrS 22/20 and 86/36 immediately supply relatives or jinn as agents in a separate taking clause. No agent is overt in the disappearance clause itself.
PrS 15/59, 22/19-20 and 45/8 overlap existing examples cited under older edition numbering; no duplicate additions or unsupported citation replacements.

Confirm the Detransitive Preterit versus unprefixed Infectum and Part. Pass. distribution of mḏ̣ayəʕ/mḏ̣ayʕo/mḏ̣ayʕi, especially PrS 36/65-66, 44/59 and 65/39. Are any reduced forms active II with an intransitive use?
Verify final ḥ at PrS 18/45, 22/19, 29/25,29 and z in mzayʕo (PrS 49/52); no normalization has been made.
Is mḏ̣ayəʕ i səsto in PrS 74/40 active with the man as subject, or an agreement/text issue? The German makes the mare the subject; it was not selected.
Confirm the person/object segmentation in mḏ̣ayʕulle (JTM 1.6/2-3, PrS 86/7); the latter riddle was not used to establish a box.
Verify older PrS numbering before altering the inherited citations, including prs 128/35 versus supplied PrS 45/8.
Time can be a resource that a person causes to be lost, while hawnayḏe is the subject of Detransitive loss of awareness. The grammatical frames differ despite related semantics.
